title: Tio, and Labat's given name
summary: Labat praises Tio as a sight reader and explains he is Joseph Sumner Labat, named for his father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Dad knows what he's doing with anything he picked up. He said baritone horn, but he was playing that with us in the neighborhood. He could play that baritone horn. He's a good musician. His dad was a good baritone horn player. Yeah. His dad was one of the best. He had to play for one-year-old horn. Yeah. He had to play for one-year-old horn. Yeah. He had to play for one-year-old horn. Yeah. I'm calling him everything. Sumter. Sumter. Sumter. Sumter. Sumter. I thought it was Sumter and La Bada. Sumter. Sumter. Tio used to take me to the hummingbird on Saturday night.
You know Tio, huh? Oh, number one musician Tio was. They were beatin' vocals in there. He was one of the best I ever knew. Yeah, he was a sight reader.
They called you anything besides Sumter? Joe. Joe. I heard him call you Joe.
My name is Joseph Sumter, but most people call me Sumter, you see. My name is Joseph Sumter. And your father was Joseph? Joseph L. Bada. Same here. Same here. Same here.

Well you had an advantage of having a musical father. I'm glad to see you. I just seen how much time I had on. You got some more questions? No, I just saw some of the time I had on tape, so. Yeah, I just thought you had something special. No. Would you say there was much difference in the way the bands here played and the way they played in New Orleans? Yeah, and you just fit right in. There couldn't be too much difference, you know. That's right.
